note: Tome Sync serialises content/config/files to flat files. drush tome:export / tome:import move everything; tome:export-content <type:id> exports a single entity to tome_content_directory (default ../content) as <entity_type>.<uuid>.json. No config object; directories are settings.php keys (tome_content_directory, tome_files_directory, tome_sync_encoder json|yaml). File handling is the swappable tome_sync.file_sync service (override with NullFileSync). Partial imports use the tome_sync_content_hash table. Permission 'use tome sync' gates the UI at /admin/config/tome/sync. Medium introspects node 1's on-disk export filename (setup exports node 1). Hard re-exports node 1 and verifies the JSON file. Grounded in existing node:1 (uuid 5528817f-2211-4569-91a2-af6f5da9da25); no fixtures created, no page rendering. NOTE: this site's tome_sync_content_hash table had been dropped by a prior run and was restored (drupal_install_schema) so tome:export-content completes cleanly.

evals.prompt: Using Tome Sync, what is the workflow to rebuild a Drupal site from its flat-file content export on a fresh database? Name the two key Drush commands.
evals.expected_output: Do the initial export once with 'drush tome:export'. To rebuild: reinstall Drupal ('drush si <profile> -y') then run 'drush tome:import' to import all config, content, and files from disk.

evals.prompt: Where does Tome Sync write exported content, and how do you switch the export format from JSON to YAML?
evals.expected_output: Content is written to tome_content_directory (default ../content) as <entity_type>.<uuid>.json. Set $settings['tome_sync_encoder'] = 'yaml' in settings.php to use the experimental YAML encoder (default is json). These are settings.php values, not a config object.

evals.prompt: I don't want Tome Sync to copy/delete my files on every export because I symlink my files directory. How can I change Tome Sync's file-handling behavior?
evals.expected_output: Override the tome_sync.file_sync service in your site services.yml to use Drupal\tome_sync\NullFileSync, which does nothing on file sync operations. (Related: 'drush tome:clean-files' removes unused exported files.)

evals.prompt: This site has Tome Sync content exports on disk. Inspect the content export directory and give the exact JSON filename Tome Sync uses for node 1's exported content.
evals.expected_output: node.5528817f-2211-4569-91a2-af6f5da9da25.json — Tome Sync names content files <entity_type>.<uuid>.json in the tome_content_directory (../content). node 1's uuid is 5528817f-2211-4569-91a2-af6f5da9da25.

evals.prompt: Using Tome Sync on this site, export the content entity 'node 1' to the on-disk JSON content store and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Run 'drush tome:export-content node:1'. Tome Sync writes content/node.5528817f-2211-4569-91a2-af6f5da9da25.json as valid JSON in the tome_content_directory.
